title: Course objectives, outcomes and requirements: ideas from other products
intro: This page gathers ideas for the Objectives, Outcomes and Requirements step inside Courses in Essentials 2.0. It shows how instructors define what learners should achieve and what they need before starting. It also shows how those expectations appear in the Learner Portal, and how links are kept for later assessment. Competency setup, scenarios, sharing and Canvas delivery sit in neighbouring modules. The examples come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero. The notes separate controls we can see on screen from behaviour we could not verify.

questions.title: Are objectives structured as list items, not free text, and can they be reordered?
questions.answer: On Udemy, instructors write course outcomes as separate required fields, with 'Add more' and a remaining-character counter for each line. Teachable uses repeated add and delete fields for optional checkout bullet points. That is a similar layout for marketing text, not a formal outcome model. Neither screenshot shows reordering. For Essentials, separate outcome items are well supported. Whether instructors can move items and keep that order is a design decision, not something these examples prove.

questions.title: Do learners see objectives in the same shape the instructor wrote them?
questions.answer: Udemy tells instructors that their 'Intended learners' descriptions will appear publicly. Separate learner screenshots show outcome checklists. Coursera shows checked outcomes on desktop and module text on mobile. These are not matched author and learner views of the same course, so the screenshots do not show whether the wording and order match. In Teachable's student preview sequence, draft curriculum can exist in admin while the student view is empty. Essentials needs a preview that shows both whether content is published and what the learner actually sees.

questions.title: Are requirements and prerequisites enforced, or only informational, and how is that shown?
questions.answer: Udemy puts prerequisite descriptions in their own authoring field with a concrete readiness example, but no admission rule is shown. Keep entry readiness, progression locks and completion rules distinct. Kajabi can lock a module until a selected lesson is complete, and it says an assessment must be passed. Codecademy states that learners must watch all content and score at least 70% to complete; what happens when they fail was not tested. Skillshare shows 'Beginner' level and skills next to 'Watch Now'. Uxcel pairs beginner-friendly guidance with an enrollment path and a separate paid upgrade prompt. Those last two screenshots do not show a learning prerequisite being enforced. A requirement description must not quietly imply an access rule.

questions.title: Can objectives be linked to a lesson, assessment or competency later?
questions.answer: Udemy places an objective with a curriculum section above nested content. It does not show reusable course-outcome links to individual assessments or competencies. Asana gives the clearest general linking flow: no connected project, then a searchable picker, then a connected project with weight and progress. Its automatic progress summary is a similar idea from another product type. It is not evidence that finishing a project proves learning. Essentials should keep a linkable objective identity, and leave competency setup and scenario mapping to their neighbouring modules.

questions.title: What guidance helps authors write objectives (examples, verb prompts, character limits, AI suggestions)?
questions.answer: Udemy makes writing limits visible: at least four outcomes, and a remaining-character counter on each item. Udemy also supplies a prerequisite example explaining that prior programming experience is unnecessary. That guides readiness wording, not a measurable learning outcome. Asana asks authors how they will define success and offers AI improvement in its goal flow. A separate Asana onboarding screen explains choices and allows uncertainty. Kajabi generates a course outline, then shows editable results with 'Apply' and 'Discard'. That review control is useful. No example here shows coaching on action verbs or AI checking whether a learning objective is measurable. Treat that kind of support as an Essentials proposal, not a pattern shared across these products.

questions.title: Where does this step sit in course creation: required up front, or optional later?
questions.answer: Udemy puts 'Intended learners' first under 'Plan your course' and requires at least four outcomes. The screenshot does not show what happens if someone tries to submit with fewer. Teachable's course flow goes from the Setup guide through confirmation and launch success to Published, without showing an objective step. Kajabi's creation steps show generation and appearance stages, but do not place outcome authoring. Those screenshots cannot prove that outcomes are optional. For Essentials, define what must be finished before publish separately from the order in which an instructor may draft the course.

references.title: Course setup bullet fields
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable shows separate optional bullet fields with add and delete controls. No control to reorder them is visible.

references.title: Checkout bullets, filled and empty
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable shows filled and empty checkout bullet fields in the same repeated layout. How they are stored, and whether they can be reordered, is not shown.

references.title: 'Intended learners' outcomes step
references.question: Q1
references.take: Udemy requires at least four separate outcomes, shows a remaining-character counter, and offers 'Add more'. It also says the statements appear publicly. Reordering is not shown.

references.title: Course page 'What you'll learn'
references.question: Q2
references.take: Coursera shows learners a checked outcomes list. Whether the author's exact text and order are kept is not shown.

references.title: Mobile course outcomes view
references.question: Q2
references.take: On mobile, Coursera shows module-level syllabus text. That is not evidence of the same objective list the author wrote.

references.title: Curriculum student preview
references.question: Q2
references.take: Teachable offers 'Preview as student'. In this sequence the learner curriculum is empty because only published content appears (screens 1 to 3).

references.title: Landing page learning outcomes
references.question: Q2
references.take: Udemy's course landing page has a dedicated learning outcomes area for learners. Expected achievement is easy to scan before enrollment.

references.title: Course outcomes as checklist
references.question: Q2
references.take: A second Udemy course view shows outcomes as separate items learners can read. Objectives appear as a checklist.

references.title: 'About this course' on mobile
references.question: Q2
references.take: On Udemy mobile, course outcomes appear under 'More', then 'About this course' (screens 1 to 2). How closely they match the authoring screen is not shown.

references.title: Completion criteria stated
references.question: Q3
references.take: Codecademy states completion criteria: watch all content and score at least 70%. The screenshot does not show a failure or a blocked path.

references.title: Module lock on lesson completion
references.question: Q3
references.take: Kajabi can lock a module until a selected lesson is complete. Assessment completion requires a pass.

references.title: Level shown beside Watch Now
references.question: Q3
references.take: Skillshare presents requirements as information on the course page, separate from the enrollment controls.

references.title: Requirements text for authors
references.question: Q3
references.take: Udemy asks authors for public requirements or prerequisites text, including skills, experience, tools or equipment. The field is informational and does not prove enforced admission.

references.title: Beginner-friendly enrollment path
references.question: Q3
references.take: Uxcel shows beginner-friendly readiness messaging and open enrollment. The Pro membership prompt is a paid upgrade, not a learning prerequisite.

references.title: Goal linked to a project
references.question: Q4
references.take: Asana connects a goal to a project: from none linked, through project search, to a connected row with a progress summary (screens 1 to 3). This is a similar idea from another product type.

references.title: Section learning objective
references.question: Q4
references.take: Udemy attaches a learning objective to a curriculum section that holds nested lectures and content. It does not prove mapping to an individual lesson, assessment or competency.

references.title: Objective choices in onboarding
references.question: Q5
references.take: Asana onboarding explains three objective choices and offers an unsure option. This guides a choice; it is not a measurable learning-objective editor.

references.title: AI course generator prompt
references.question: Q5
references.take: Kajabi shows a focused Course generator dialog with a topic field and a 'Generate' action. AI assistance can start from a single authoring prompt.

references.title: Editable generated outline
references.question: Q5
references.take: Kajabi generates editable course structure and descriptions for review. It does not show learning objectives being generated.

references.title: Lesson editor AI assistant
references.question: Q5
references.take: Teachable places an AI assistant beside lesson content. No objective-specific prompt or generated outcome is visible.

references.title: Prerequisite placeholder example
references.question: Q5
references.take: Udemy provides an explicit prerequisite placeholder example. It does not model a measurable learning outcome.

references.title: Creation steps in progress
references.question: Q6
references.take: Kajabi visibly generates an outline, landing page and email in sequence. No objective step is shown.

references.title: Optional course appearance step
references.question: Q6
references.take: Kajabi explicitly makes the thumbnail optional. That does not show whether outcomes are optional.

references.title: Course setup guide page
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable's course Setup guide puts curriculum creation first, then customization and pricing on one page. 'Publish your course' stays visible.

references.title: Course published confirmation
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable confirms launch in a dialog with a sales page link and a 'Done' action. Publication is clearly separate from earlier editing steps.

references.title: Publish section only
references.question: Q6
references.take: This three-screen sequence shows publishing a curriculum section only. No objective requirement is visible (screens 1 to 3).

references.title: Setup through published course
references.question: Q6
references.take: This four-screen sequence shows course setup through to published, without an objective step (screens 1 to 4).
